glossary.definition: The feeling, color, or line that remains after a song, page, or screening ends.
A version allowed to be visibly unfinished: a sound, thought, or page before it is corrected into silence.
A place reserved for work that deserves time before it receives a final title or conclusion.
A small observation that may not be the main work, but changes how the main work is read.

processFrames.title: The first loose page
processFrames.description: A space for a lyric fragment, an image, or an early line before the work has found its shape.

processFrames.title: The sound beside it
processFrames.description: A space for a voice-note still, a rehearsal image, or the object that kept a piece moving.

processFrames.title: What stayed unfinished
processFrames.description: A space for the alternate title, crossed-out line, or future question that belongs beside the finished work.

toolkit.title: A three-word weather note
toolkit.description: Before making, name the room in three ordinary words. Let those words guide the first ten minutes.

toolkit.title: One object, one page
toolkit.description: Choose the nearest object and write only what it remembers. Do not explain the whole day.

toolkit.title: The return question
toolkit.description: At the end of a session, leave one honest question that makes it easier to come back tomorrow.

audioPostcard.title: A note from 2:17 AM
audioPostcard.description: A short instrumental fragment held here as a listening-room postcard, for the kind of return that does not need an explanation.
